canonical_name: Bannai-Ito fixed-valency finiteness conjecture for distance-regular graphs
literal_source_claim_en: A bound on the diameter of distance-regular graphs.
source_attribution: Eiichi Bannai and Tatsuro Ito, 1984 (catalog metadata; original conjecture locator reported as Algebraic Combinatorics I, p. 237)
canonical_statement: For every fixed valency greater than two, there are only finitely many distance-regular graphs.
canonical_claim: For every fixed valency greater than two, there are only finitely many distance-regular graphs.
statement_blocker: The catalog gives an unspecified diameter-bound gloss rather than the standard fixed-valency finiteness statement. The proof source identifies the named theorem and explains a diameter-bound reduction, but the original 1984 page, incorporated definitions, exact gloss relationship, correction/errata audit, independent source approval, distance-regularity encoding, isomorphism-class finiteness representation, canonical Lean expression, fingerprints, transports, and mutations remain open.
domain_and_universes: Prospective named root: each natural valency k >= 3 and finite connected loopless undirected distance-regular graphs, classified up to graph isomorphism. The vertex-carrier universe, small representative universe, quotient or Fin-normal-form encoding, finiteness predicate, decidability data, and intersection-number representation remain open.
quantifiers: for every natural valency k greater than two
there are only finitely many distance-regular graph isomorphism classes of valency k
